MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  PALOS VERDES ESTATES, CALIFORNIA
  July 10, 2012

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Palos Verdes Estates was called to order
this day at 7:30 PM in the Council Chambers of City Hall by Mayor Bird.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

ROLL CALL

PRESENT:  Mayor Bird, Mayor Pro Tem Goodhart, Councilmember Humphrey,
  Councilmember Perkins, Councilmember Rea

ABSENT:  None

ALSO PRESENT:  City Manager Smith, Police Chief Dreiling, Public Works Director Rigg, City
  Treasurer Sherwood, City Attorney Hogin, Asst. to City Manager Davis,
  Asst./Deputy City Clerk Kroneberger

MAYOR'S REPORT - MATTERS OF COMMUNITY INTEREST

CONSENT AGENDA (ITEMS 1 - 3)

On motion of Councilmember Humphrey, seconded by Councilmember Perkins, Council approved
CONSENT AGENDA (Items 1 - 3) by unanimous oral vote.

1.  WAIVE FURTHER READING

2.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF JUNE 26, 2012

3.  DESIGNATION OF VOTING DELEGATE AND ALTERNATE - LEAGUE OF
  CALIFORNIA CITIES ANNUAL BUSINESS MEETING

COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC – No one came forward to speak.

PUBLIC HEARINGS - 7:30 PM

4.  APPEAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION APPROVAL OF NC-1440/GA-1492-12;
  NEIGHBORHOOD COMPATIBILITY AND GRADING APPLICATIONS FOR A
  NEW SINGLE FAMILY RESIDENCE LOCATED AT 968 VIA RINCON-LOT 5,
  BLOCK 1731, TRACT 7142; APPELLANT: JOHN & LENORE DELUCA

CITY COUNCIL
July 10, 2012

  1
 Mayor Bird recused himself from consideration of Items #4 and #5, determined by Council
consensus to be heard concurrently, turned the gavel over to MPT Goodhart, and left Chambers.

Planning Director Rigg reported that the Planning Commission approved the project with various
conditions and it was appealed by two neighbors. The appellants’ primary concern was for view
impacts primarily due to new chimneys atop the home. Since the appeal was filed, the applicant
and appellants have met and agreed to a modified plan and created a mutually agreed upon
condition: the existing 2 ft. 10 in. by 5 ft. 7 in. north chimney is to be modified to 2 ft. 6 in. by 3 ft.
6 in.; and the existing 3 ft. by 5 ft. 6 in. south chimney shall be modified to 2 ft. 6 in. by 3 ft. 6
inches. He stated that the owner and appellants have all verbally approved a drawing.

Councilmember Rea confirmed with Director Rigg that the agreed measurements represent the
horizontal dimensions with no change to the vertical dimensions. The height of the chimneys
cannot change because it is the minimum allowed per the Building Code.

MPT Goodhart confirmed with Director Rigg that the chimneys would face both north and south.

MPT Goodhart opened the public hearing.

Alex Cornelius, representative retained by the appellants, the DeLuca and Dotson families, stated
that they met with architect Tomaro; Mr. Moore, the owner; and the owner’s counsel, Mr. Lundy.
He confirmed the condition, as described by Director Rigg, was acceptable to both appellants.

Albro Lundy, representing Darren Moore, owner, concurred that they have met and agreed upon
the resolution as proposed.

MPT Goodhart closed the public hearing.

Councilmember Humphrey said she appreciated the neighbors providing the opportunity to view
the impacts from each of their homes, and thanked everyone involved for working out their
disagreements.

Councilmember Rea commented that it was to the advantage of the involved parties to determine
an acceptable solution; Council may have provided a different solution. It is a lesson that shows
the importance of meeting, conferring and working it out before coming to the decision making
body, and he commended everyone for their time and hard work.

Councilmember Perkins concurred. She said this process embodies the challenge for homeowners
to find balance in building what they would like with being a good neighbor and complying with
Neighborhood Compatibility. She commended the Planning Commission for their work, and the
applicant and appellants for the work they did to come up with a solution. This solution may not
have been an option Council would have considered not was it an option she had considered upon
visiting the properties. Chimneys and vents, and their aesthetics will be looked at further as we go
on.

CITY COUNCIL
July 10, 2012

  2
 MPT Goodhart thanked the homeowners for the opportunity to look at views and impacts from
their homes; he was pleased they were all able to come to an agreement.

On motion of Councilmember Perkins, seconded by Councilmember Rea, Council confirmed the
Planning Commission’s Approval of NC-1440/GA-1492-12; Neighborhood Compatibility and
Grading Applications for a New Single Family Residence Located at 968 Via Rincon-Lot 5, Block
1731, Tract 7142; Appellant: John & Lenore DeLuca, as conditioned, with the additional condition
that the existing 2 ft. 10 in. by 5 ft. 7 in. north chimney shall be modified to 2 ft. 6 in. by 3 ft. 6 in.;
and the existing 3 ft. 10 in. by 5 ft. 6 in. south chimney shall be modified to 2 ft. 6 in. by 3 ft. 6
inches, by unanimous oral vote; Bird recused.

5.  APPEAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION APPROVAL OF NC-1440/GA-1492-12;
  NEIGHBORHOOD COMPATIBILITY AND GRADING APPLICATIONS FOR A
  NEW SINGLE FAMILY RESIDENCE LOCATED AT 968 VIA RINCON-LOT 5,
  BLOCK 1731, TRACT 7142; APPELLANT: GENE & LINDA DOTSON

On motion of Councilmember Perkins, seconded by Councilmember Rea, Council confirmed the
Planning Commission’s Approval of NC-1440/GA-1492-12; Neighborhood Compatibility and
Grading Applications for a New Single Family Residence Located at 968 Via Rincon-Lot 5, Block
1731, Tract 7142; Appellant: Gene & Linda Dotson, as conditioned, with the additional condition
that the existing 2 ft. 10 in. by 5 ft. 7 in. north chimney shall be modified to 2 ft. 6 in. by 3 ft. 6 in.;
and the 3 ft. 10 in. by 5 ft. 6 in. south chimney shall be modified to 2 ft. 6 in. by 3 ft. 6 inches, by
unanimous oral vote; Bird recused.

Mayor Bird returned to Chambers at 7:53 p.m.

6.  INTRODUCE AND ADOPT THE 2012 SELF-CERTIFICATION RESOLUTION R12-
  18; ADOPTING THE LOCAL DEVELOPMENT REPORT FOR THE CONGESTION
  MANAGEMENT PROGRAM

Deputy City Clerk Kroneberger confirmed that public notice was given.

Director Rigg reported that The Traffic Congestion Relief and Spending Act of 1990 was passed by
voters, and the Congestion Management Plan was subsequently developed. One factor of
compliance is that the City must adopt a local development report on an annual basis. 14 new
homes were developed within the last year and 11 were demolished, with a net increase of 3 homes.
At a meeting he and MPT Goodhart attended, it was determined the program in its current form
will be eliminated. The County is working towards a congestion mitigation fee on the net
development within the City. Additional fees will be required to help mitigate congestion caused
by new projects.

Councilmember Rea asked staff how that program would be funded. Director Rigg responded that
the funds will come from City-assessed fees paid along with building permits by individual
homeowners-- ranging from $3000 per unit to potentially $12,000. The fees go toward paying for
regional projects, such as intersection improvement at PV Drive North. City Manager Smith said
the fee would be based on a trip reduction calculation; the money would remain locally to fund
CITY COUNCIL
July 10, 2012

  3
 local congestion management projects. Director Rigg said the $3000 calculation is based on $300
per trip at 10 trips per residence.

MPT Goodhart said some cities elected not to collect this fee because they want to encourage
residential development, but rather would collect the fees for business development. Mayor Bird
confirmed with staff that the County would still assess the development fees to the City.

Councilmember Perkins said the County is experiencing different levels of willingness to assess
fees; the process is being presented to different local government agencies, such as the COG.

MPT Goodhart said areas and cities that are largely built out along the coastline, like PVE, are not
going to have a lot of net development. Inland cities will likely be more affected.

Councilmember Rea confirmed that the charges would only apply to new units, not additions, with
MPT Goodhart.

Mayor Bird opened public hearing, received no public input, and closed the public hearing.

On motion of MPT Goodhart, seconded by Councilmember Rea, Council introduced and adopted
the 2012 Self-Certification Resolution R12-18; adopting the Local Development Report for the
Congestion Management Program by unanimous oral vote.

OLD BUSINESS

NEW BUSINESS

7.  REVIEW AND APPROVAL OF THE FY 2012-13 PALOS VERDES STABLE BUDGET
  AND ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION R12-17 APPROVING INCREASE IN BOARD
  FEES

City Manager Smith reported that HGS Management has operated the PVE Stable since March
2009 under a Council-approved concession agreement. Council liaisons Goodhart and Humphrey
met with Stable management on June 11th to review the projected results for this current fiscal year
and proposed budget for FY 12-13. For the current year, the operator is projecting a net income of
$82,300 on revenue of $620,000 and expenditures of $537,700. This performance is slightly less
than what the adopted budget projected and audit results for FY 10-11. The stable is audited by the
City's independent auditors, which include required reports of capital improvements.

City Manager Smith said the budget variance for the current fiscal year income is $32,000 higher
across all revenue categories – boarders, trainers’ fees, and supplemental services. Expenditures
increased in personnel costs, hay/hay substitution, repairs, and certain legal fees. This year, the
operator incurred capital improvement costs of $10,775 for the first phase of an arena lighting
project (new lights are proposed for the FY 12-13 budget) and equipment costs of $11,000
compared to a zero budget, with an additional $7,000 in facility repairs that were over and above
the approved budget. For FY 12-13, revenue of $614,000 is projected with expenditures of

CITY COUNCIL
July 10, 2012

  4
 $574,000 for a net income of $40,000.

The budget proposes a $25/month board increase for both box and in/out stalls to be effective
August 1st. Pipe stall costs would remain unchanged. This increase follows an increase that
Council approved for last fiscal year that ranged $35-$50. Rates comparisons of local facilities
were provided within the staff report. The proposed increases are to partly offset costs of hay,
which has doubled since FY 10-11 when the cost was $85/horse/month; currently, it is
$170/month. Part of the increase in hay was recouped last year; with part of the proposed board
increase to recoup part of that balance.

The FY 12-13 budget includes a placeholder of $24,000 for capital improvements, such as arena
lighting; opportunities for efficiency lighting with the assistance of the South Bay Energy Savings
Center (SBESC) will be sought. There is $135,000 in the City stable fund (concession fee
proceeds) that could be made available to partner and help the operator undertake some
improvements. The intent is to return to Council in late fall with a more detailed capital program.
The concessionaire pays a 5% fee to City, which is projected to generate $30,700 in next year’s
budget.

David Mclewee, HGS Management, concessionaire, stated the reason for a proposed $25 increase
was primarily for the cost of hay (originally $8.75; now up to $18-$18.50 per bale), which has been
fluctuating greatly. Fortunately, revenues have increased to bear some of those added costs. He
stated he may have not provided enough time for boarders to consider the proposed rate increases.
He requested that Council leave the fees as they are at this time to provide more opportunity for
response from boarders. They would also present proposals for capital improvements at a later date.
The notice to boarders was posted, but not mailed. He said he personally spoke to about 17
boarders; many were surprised at the increased cost of hay and how much is used.

Mayor Bird said he appreciated that the June 28th notice advised boarders that the increases would
be discussed at this evening’s meeting, providing an opportunity for them to speak.

Councilmember Humphrey confirmed with Mr. Mclewee that he is proposing to return with a
capital improvement plan at such time Council will consider the increases again. She confirmed
although many were aware, an updated notice should be mailed to boarders. City Manager Smith
confirmed that the content of the notice is accurate, but could go out with the new proposed
effective date.

Councilmember Rea confirmed with City Manager Smith that Council can approve the budget as
presented this evening, and opt not to adopt the resolution which would effectuate the fee increase.
The concessionaire could return later with a more detailed capital program with a possible
amendment, and resolution approving the fee changes at that time. Mayor Bird asked if adoption
would affect the accuracy of the budget. City Manager Smith said it does affect the net operating
position, but they could modify the budget to accurately reflect the individual categories this fall.

Councilmember Humphrey supported approving the budget and making modifications later.

Mayor Bird asked Mr. Mclewee the proposed effective date for fee increases. Mr. Mclewee
CITY COUNCIL
July 10, 2012

  5
 suggested January 1st.

Councilmember Perkins said she appreciated a delay in fee increases until everyone has had fair
and adequate notice. Mr. Mclewee confirmed the notice had been posted on the Stable notice
board, but they would mail a notice as well.

MPT Goodhart confirmed with City Manager Smith that the local boarding rate comparisons are
current, although it is unknown if the Peter Weber Equestrian Center in RHE, which just
transitioned from a city department to a concession operation, will consider increases at another
time this year. She confirmed that all City concessions generally provide a 30-day notice when fee
changes are considered.

MPT Goodhart asked Mr. Mclewee about the monthly impact of cost increases on the stable’s
operation. Mr. Mclewee said the costs have nearly doubled to ~$11,000/month since 2009. He
described several factors that have been pushing up prices for hay. MPT Goodhart asked what other
additional costs they’ve experienced. Mr. Mclewee said there have been increases in Workers
Comp and payroll costs.

Councilmember Rea confirmed that monthly bills are mailed to boarders, and notices can be
included. Mr. Mclewee said notices were mailed to boarders for interest in Stable Committee
participation, which is to include a resident and non-resident boarder, but had no response.

Mayor Bird commented that a 6 month delay in increases would be impactful.

Councilmember Humphrey said she appreciated that a letter notice was posted where it could be
seen by boarders, and that Mr. Mclewee also spoke to numerous boarders personally. She
supported sending a notice out with billing statements so that everyone is informed.

Councilmember Perkins said she was concerned about the affect a delay would have on the budget
and asked if it is sound to wait until January 1st for the increase. City Manager Smith said she
anticipated returning to Council this fall, such as the first meeting in October.

MPT Goodhart said he had been concerned that the previous Stable concessionaire operated at a net
or negative income. Although it is admirable to delay a boarding increase, he was concerned
delaying to January 1st is too long and supported returning to Council in October. Mr. Mclewee
said returning in October is fine and helpful.

Councilmember Humphrey said it is also important for everyone to know the reasons for the
increases are based on cost increases. Mr. Mclewee agreed.

Mayor Bird thanked Mr. Mclewee for attending the joint meeting with other City concessions
earlier in the month.

Councilmember Perkins complimented Mr. Mclewee on making strides in filling stalls and making
it a thriving barn. She said when reviewing capital systems, working with SBESC should be a must
to assist in achieving more effective and energy efficient lighting. She said RHE has utilized
CITY COUNCIL
July 10, 2012

  6
 SBESC's services.

Mayor Bird agreed. Discussion of common interests amongst concessionaires, such as energy
efficiency and outdoor lighting, can be helpful.

Council consensus was to approve the proposed budget this evening, but to not take action on the
resolution.

On motion of Councilmember Rea, seconded by MPT Goodhart, Council reviewed and approved
the FY 2012-13 Palos Verdes Stable Budget by unanimous oral vote.

STAFF REPORTS

8.  CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

City Manager Smith reported that it was her pleasure to announce the appointment of Captain John
Eberhard as the City's 9th Police Chief. Captain Eberhard has served his entire law enforcement
career with Palos Verdes Estates and knows the community very well. He was the initial and only
coordinator of the PVE-CARES program, directing the group of volunteers. She said the
appointment is effective October 1, 2012. Chief Dreiling will remain in office until then to provide
mentoring and will swear-in the new Chief at the September 25th City Council Meeting.

Mayor Bird congratulated Chief-designate John Eberhard.

DEMANDS

9.  DEMANDS OF JULY 10, 2012

On motion of Councilmember Rea, seconded by Councilmember Humphrey, Council authorized
payment of Motion #1 – Payroll Warrant of July 6, 2012, totaling $218,721.84; Motion #2 –
Warrant Register of July 10, 2012 (FY11-12), totaling $108,132.76; and Motion #2a – Warrant
Register of July 10, 2012 (FY12-13), totaling $373,309.04 by unanimous oral vote.

MAYOR& CITY COUNCILMEMBERS' REPORTS

Mayor Bird introduced Community Relations Officer Marcelle McCullough and welcomed her to
the City. Ms. McCullough reported that Neighborhood Watch installed a new Board, and is
interviewing for NW Newsletter editor-in-chief. Annual membership dues are $5 and Mayor Bird
encouraged residents to join, or to contact Ms. McCullough at PVEPD for more information.

Ms. McCullough announced that National Night Out is scheduled for the evening of August 7th,
and the City will also host a Disaster Preparedness Fair on September 22nd.

Mayor Bird reported on his attendance and presentation of a proclamation, with Council
representatives, to honor outgoing chair, Councilmember Perkins, at the June 28th COG Board
Meeting. Councilmember Perkins thanked the Council, the City Manager, and Asst. to the City
CITY COUNCIL
July 10, 2012

  7
 Manager for participating. Councilmember Humphrey congratulated Councilmember Perkins on
her term as COG chair, and thanked Mayor Bird for including Council in his presentation to Ms.
Perkins.

Mayor Bird reported that Saturday with the Mayor at City Hall on July 7th was well attended and
thanked CRO McCullough for her participation.

Councilmember Rea reported that he and Mayor Bird are attending the L.A. Brown Act
Educational Forum, hosted by the Los Angeles County Prosecutors Association and the Los
Angeles County District Attorney's Criminal Justice Institute at the MTA offices in Los Angeles on
Wednesday, July 11th.

Council commented on the 4th of July event at Malaga Cove School and congratulated Mayor Bird
for winning the apple pie contest. Mayor Bird congratulated the event chairs for another successful
Independence Day event.

Councilmember Rea reported that he will be attending and giving a presentation at the California
Joint Powers Insurance Authority Annual Risk Management meeting in San Francisco on
November 7th – 9th.

ADJOURNMENT

Mayor Bird adjourned the meeting at 8:33 p.m. to Tuesday, July 24, 2012 in Council Chambers of
City Hall for the purpose of a Regular Meeting.

  RESPECTFULLY SUBMITTED,

  VICKIE KRONEBERGER,
  EXECUTIVE ASSISTANT/DEPUTY CITY CLERK

APPROVED BY:

GEORGE F. BIRD, JR., MAYOR

CITY COUNCIL
July 10, 2012

  8
